mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes and then dividing the cell made the distinction between those stages clear. The division ring also connected the process to the actin and myosin encountered in muscle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the developing red cells to the body was straightforward, but the separate incorporation step felt less informative than the preceding kidney-to-marrow signal.

surprise.text: The low-oxygen cue clarified why the kidney sends a signal to support red-cell production in marrow.

arbitrary.text: I guessed that the two bone cell types would combine directly. The feedback instead showed that removal occurs in the body first; the required order was not clear to me beforehand.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the chapter connected cell division and blood production to the working body, and I would be interested to see more such connections.
